image_query: Kumbh Mela pilgrims bathing Ganges Haridwar aerial
tweets: The Kumbh Mela gathers at four sites — Prayāgrāj, Haridwār, Ujjain, Nāsik — where legend holds that drops of amṛta, nectar of immortality, fell during the Samudra Manthan. Each site hosts its Mela roughly every twelve years, timed by Jupiter's orbit.

Crowds at the Kumbh swell past 100 million over weeks — vast enough that satellites have photographed the tent cities from orbit. UNESCO inscribed it as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2017. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
